{{short description|English mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=August 2019}}
'''William Payne''' (unknown – c. 1779)  was an English mathematician<ref name="Courtney">Courtney, ''A bibliography'', p. 74.</ref> and the author of books about mathematics, [[draughts]], and [[whist]]. Payne was the brother of prominent London bookseller [[Thomas Payne (publisher)|Thomas Payne]], who sold his works and published some of them.<ref name="Courtney" /><ref name="Hanley" /><ref name="Boswell">Boswell, p. 192.</ref>

Payne's first book, ''An Introduction to the Game of Draughts'', was published in 1756.<ref name="Courtney" /><ref name="Hanley">Hanley, p. 181.</ref>  The dedication and preface were written by [[Samuel Johnson]].<ref name="Hanley" /><ref name="Boswell" />

Payne's second book, ''An Introduction to Geometry: Containing the Most Useful Propositions in Euclid, & Other Authors'', was published in 1767.<ref>Payne, William (1767). ''An Introduction to Geometry: Containing the Most Useful Propositions in Euclid, & Other Authors''. London: H. Hart.</ref>

The book ''Maxims for Playing the Game of Whist; With All Necessary Calculations, and Laws of the Game'' was published anonymously in 1773; published by his brother Thomas, it is believed to have been written by William Payne.<ref>Courtney, ''English whist'', p. 360.</ref>
